label: In code or technical writing, the list data type: an empty list being created ([] or list(), ArrayList, vector, a JavaScript array), an item appended or pushed onto a list, a List type hint, a list comprehension, or prose saying a function is or returns a list (the word 'array' in prose fires more weakly). The word 'list' in everyday or non-programming senses (a ship listing, a stock listing, shopping or guest lists) stays quiet, as do dicts, sets and tuples in the same code. A variable whose name contains 'list' fires moderately even when it does not hold a list.

probed_before.source: this checkout's .probe-log, before the pre-registration commit

qc.label_under_test: In code (Python, JavaScript, Java, C++ and similar), a list or array being started, typed or grown: strongest for an empty list literal or empty list constructor that is about to be filled, a List/ArrayList/vector type or type hint, or adding one item to the end of it (append, push); a list literal that already holds items fires more weakly, and so does technical prose saying something returns a list or array. Dicts, sets, tuples, plain numbers and 'list' in everyday prose stay quiet; a variable only named with 'list' can fire weakly.
